University of Nebraska-Lincoln
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Select MS/PhD when applying from a bachelor’s degree with doctoral intent.
• International TA preparation can require arrival in late July.
• Admission English exemption does not establish exemption from teaching certification.
• Brian Harbourne, Luchezar Avramov, Roger Wiegand and Sylvia Wiegand are explicitly emeritus on the
current group page. Existing advising does not establish availability for a new 2027 student [faculty_group].
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Applicants completing a bachelor’s degree can seek the doctoral track. Mathematics favors GPA 3.0 or higher
and substantial proof-based coursework but describes no absolute departmental GPA cutoff. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s applicants intending a doctorate are strongly urged to select MS/PhD, rather than PhD only;
evaluation is the same and the combined route avoids a later master’s application fee. There is no separate
mathematics application or aid form. Prepare international Financial Resource Certification; its precise
submission stage requires confirmation. [s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser commitment is needed. Students receive an initial academic adviser and choose a
research adviser later. [s2]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use CollegeNET, then the status page at https://go.unl.edu/gradappstatus for checklist, alternate uploads,
recommender reminders/replacement, and accepting or declining a decision. Only one unsubmitted application
may be open at a time. [s1] [s6]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
The mathematics application page explicitly identifies January 15, 2027 for Fall 2027 support consideration. [s1]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Mathematics lists TOEFL 100 and IELTS 7.5, but its FAQ says above 7.5; confirm the IELTS boundary.
International teaching preparation has separate oral requirements: old TOEFL speaking 22 or IELTS speaking
6.5 to enter the three-week summer ITA program, followed by a teaching assessment. New TOEFL-scale
departmental thresholds were not located. [s1] [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
An earned bachelor’s or higher degree from an accredited institution using English as the instructional
language exempts admission English testing. In-progress degree timing is not explicit. The international
teaching assessment/training rules remain separate. [s1] [s4]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Recommended, not required. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required; no separate recommendation or no-consideration rule was established. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three required; up to five allowed. Choose writers who can assess mathematical ability. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship references; Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
This specific reference detail was not established by the public program/graduate application instructions
checked. Confirm it in the current referee-help screen or with admissions before entering contacts; no
invitation was triggered during research. [s1] [s2] [s6]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
After entering referee contact information in CollegeNET, the applicant can send a secure recommendation
link. The sources do not say that mere entry automatically sends it. [s1]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The graduate application status checklist tracks missing materials and permits recommender reminders or
replacement. Letter receipt should be checked there. [s6]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
The status portal permits replacing recommenders. Replacement of an already uploaded letter and reuse
across cycles are not explained publicly. [s6]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
A nine-month GTA carries full tuition and 79% of the health-insurance premium; the student pays 21% plus
student fees. No exact stipend dollar amount was established from the public mathematics pay information
checked. [s3]
Years of support [Unresolved]
This particular funding term was not established by the public program/admissions material checked. Obtain
the exact rule in the funding offer or from the graduate coordinator; neither eligibility nor a guaranteed
amount/duration is inferred from silence. [s1] [s2] [s6]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants can receive assistantship funding. Students from non-English-speaking countries
seeking support ordinarily enter in fall and attend the late-July to mid-August ITA program; failure of the
teaching assessment can lead to lower-paid grading duties. [s1]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Typical duties are 13-15 hours/week, at most four classroom periods plus preparation, grading, and office
hours. Summer employment is not guaranteed, although the department reports historically accommodating
nearly all interested students. [s3]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate aid form; timely complete admission applications receive automatic fellowship consideration. [s1]
[s3]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Othmer awards are described as USD 4,000-8,000/year for three years, and Chancellor awards USD 4,000/year
for two years. These are competitive supplements, not guaranteed base funding; specific citizenship
restrictions were not found. The algebra RTG announcement describes support targeted to U.S. citizens,
nationals and permanent residents; do not count it as international F-1 stipend eligibility. [s1] [rtg_international]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 50 for applicants not currently enrolled at UNL; USD 25 for currently enrolled UNL students. [s5]

Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Graduate Studies does not waive the fee, but individual programs may cover it. A mathematics-specific
international sponsorship entitlement was not found. [s5]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Mark E. Walker
Algebraic K-theory, noncommutative algebraic geometry, matrix factorizations, singularity categories, and
homological commutative algebra. [faculty1] [faculty1a]
Willa Cather Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 preprint; listed in February 2025 CV · The Hodge structure on the singularity category of a complex
hypersurface
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Alexandra Seceleanu
Geometric and computational commutative algebra, syzygies, symbolic powers and asymptotic invariants of
ideals with symmetry. [faculty3] [faculty3a]
Milton E. Mohr Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint (arXiv:2609.03131) · Symbolic Powers and Asymptotic Invariants of GL-Invariant Ideals
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Jack Jeffries
Invariant theory, differential operators, local cohomology, positive and mixed characteristic singularities, and
symbolic powers. [faculty5] [faculty5a]
Associate Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Local cohomology of modular invariant rings
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Eloísa Grifo
Symbolic powers, homological algebra, cohomological support varieties, and positive/mixed characteristic
methods. [faculty7] [faculty7a]
Associate Professor; official profile reports five current PhD advisees; new openings unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 · Bounds on cohomological support varieties
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
